analysis_plan.primary_pool: answerable categories a,b,c,d,f,g; question q1 (canonical polarity / label order); base form; first run

correctness.noul: correct iff (p>0.5 and truth) or (p<0.5 and not truth); p==0.5 counts as wrong
correctness.choice: correct iff the returned choice (argmax) equals the true label
correctness.score: correct iff argmax level of probabilities equals the true level; also MAE of expected score

calibration.log_loss: -ln p(true outcome), p clipped to [0.005, 0.995] because answers carry 2-decimal resolution
calibration.ece: 10 equal-width bins on top-label confidence (noul max(p,1-p), choice/score p_top); also P(yes) reliability for nouls

analysis_plan.selective: coverage and accuracy among answers with p_top >= t for t in {0.6,0.7,0.8,0.9,0.95,0.99}

variants.polarity: noul q2 is the negated complement; coherence s = p(q1)+p(q2); incoherent if |s-1|>0.15; contradiction if both >0.5 or both <0.5
variants.order: choice/score q2 has reversed labels/levels; flip = argmax label differs from q1; also total variation distance between label-aligned distributions
variants.solo: q1 sent alone; |delta p| vs batched q1
variants.twin: precomputed (numbers computed in code and written into the state) or rule_in_state; paired vs base

abstention.noul: 0.35 <= p <= 0.65 on unanswerable items (mid-band); also distribution of p
abstention.sufficiency_q3: p(q3) < 0.5 means 'information missing'; truth true on answerable, false on unanswerable

analysis_plan.ci: percentile bootstrap, 2000 resamples, resampling items (clusters), seed 12345

hypotheses.H1: Accuracy on compute forms is lower than on the same items with numbers precomputed (paired).
hypotheses.H2: Near-threshold (1-5%) numeric items are less accurate than far (25-300%) items.
hypotheses.H3: Among answers with p_top >= 0.9, accuracy on compute items is below 0.9; on rule-in-state items it is at least 0.9.
hypotheses.H4: Nouls on unanswerable items do not sit in the 0.35-0.65 band (they lean to 'no').
hypotheses.H5: Choices with need_more_information abstain on at least 80 % of unanswerable items.
hypotheses.H6: Polarity sums deviate from 1 more on compute items than on rule items.
